profile.summary: scPRINT is a transformer model for single-cell RNA-seq data, built mainly to infer gene networks. It takes the raw counts of a cell and can, without fine-tuning, denoise expression, produce a cell embedding, predict labels such as cell type, disease, sequencer, sex and ethnicity, and output a cell-specific gene network.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Each gene in a cell is represented by the sum of three embeddings: its identity, its expression and its genomic location. The identity embedding is the ESM2 protein embedding of the gene's most common protein product. The paper says these gene embeddings can be frozen during training or used only for initialisation. A bidirectional transformer encodes the cell. Pre-training adds three losses together: denoising (recover a profile from a downsampled one), bottleneck learning (regenerate the expression profile from the cell embedding alone) and hierarchical label prediction. scPRINT generates a gene network by selecting and combining attention heads into a gene by gene matrix.

quotes.text: scPRINT encodes the gene IDs using protein embeddings.
amino-acid embedding of its most common protein product
scPRINT’s pretraining is composed of three tasks which loss are added and optimized together: a denoising task, a bottleneck learning task, and a label prediction task.

denoising task whose goal is to recover the known transcriptomic profile from a purposefully downsampled expression profile. Bottleneck learning reconstructs the expression of requested genes using only their cell embedding.
These three embeddings are summed and then concatenated across the genes expressed in a cell
scPRINT also generates a Gene Network by selecting and combining various attention heads into a gene by gene matrix.
scPRINT can effectively be retrained with any set of gene embeddings, which can be frozen during training or used only for initialization

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The Hugging Face repository jkobject/scPRINT holds the checkpoints small-v1, small-v2, medium-v1, medium-v1.5 and large-v1, plus cell-transformer, esm-ft and many run-ID checkpoints under other_ckpts. The README uses medium-v1.5 in its examples. To reproduce the paper the README asks for version tag 1.6.4. The authors have since released scPRINT-2 in a separate repository. A result should name the checkpoint file, the Hugging Face revision and the package version.

sections.title: Intended uses
sections.body: Zero-shot expression denoising, cell embedding, cell label prediction and gene network inference on human or mouse scRNA-seq, and fine-tuning for other analyses. The README says it can be used on organisms with a similar gene set; very different organisms need new gene embeddings and retraining.

quotes.text: It is a foundation model and can be fine-tuned to perform any other analysis
scPRINT has been pretrained on both humans and mouse, and can be used on any organism with a similar gene set.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Single-cell foundation model (a large transformer) for gene network inference and zero-shot single-cell analyses.

quotes.text: scPRINT is a large transformer model built for the inference of gene networks

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Bidirectional transformer encoder with gene identity (ESM2 protein embedding), expression and genomic location embeddings, and a gene expression decoder; optional flashattention2 through triton.
facts.source_locator: Paper Fig. 1 caption; README.md: Use scPRINT

quotes.text: Schematic representation of scPRINT with its bidirectional encoder, gene expression embedding, gene location encoding, matched ESM2 protein embedding, and gene expression decoder.
If you want to be using flashattention2, know that it only supports triton 2.0

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: Raw counts in an AnnData file whose obs holds the organism ontology ID and whose var names are Ensembl IDs or HUGO symbols. Pre-training used 2200 randomly selected expressed genes per cell.

quotes.text: your anndata only needs to contain the species ontology id in its obs['organism_ontology_term_id']
contain .var_names or .var.index with gene ids defined as ENSEMBL_IDs or HUGO_SYMBOL.
scPRINT is pretrained using 2200 randomly selected expressed genes in a cell profile.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Denoised expression, cell embeddings, predicted cell labels (cell type, disease, sequencer, sex, ethnicity) and cell-specific gene networks, written as h5ad files by the command line tool.

quotes.text: predict the cell type, disease, sequencer, sex, and ethnicity of your cells
generate a gene network from any cell or cell cluster in your scRNAseq dataset
--output_filename denoised.h5ad

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 2 M to 100 M across the trained scales. Per-checkpoint counts are in the paper's Supplementary Table S2, which was not read.

quotes.text: We train scPRINT at various scales (from 2 M to 100 M parameters)

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: More than 50 million cells from the cellxgene database, from several species, diseases and ethnicities (around 80 billion tokens); human and mouse according to the README.
facts.source_locator: Paper Abstract and Results; README.md: FAQ

scPRINT has been pretrained on both humans and mouse

run_guide.summary: Install scprint, set up a lamin.ai instance, download the medium-v1.5 checkpoint and compute embeddings and label predictions for an AnnData file.
prerequisites: Python 3.10 (the version the README says was tested) and uv or pip.
A GPU is highly recommended; CPU works but is slow.
An AnnData file of raw counts with obs['organism_ontology_term_id'] and Ensembl IDs or HUGO symbols as var names.
Disk space for the lamin storage directory, which the README warns can get large.

steps.title: Create an environment and install
steps.shell:
uv venv <env-name> --python 3.10
source <env-name>/bin/activate
uv pip install scprint
steps.explanation: The README's install commands; replace <env-name>. This installs the current PyPI release, not the reviewed commit.

quotes.text: uv venv <env-name> --python 3.10
source <env-name>/bin/activate
uv pip install scprint

steps.title: Set up lamin and ontologies
steps.shell:
lamin init --storage ./testdb --name test --modules bionty
scdataloader populate all
steps.explanation: Creates a local lamin.ai instance and fills the ontologies scPRINT uses for its labels. The README says warnings here are fine.

quotes.text: lamin init --storage ./testdb --name test --modules bionty
`scdataloader populate all`

steps.title: Download a checkpoint
steps.explanation: Downloads the medium-v1.5 checkpoint from Hugging Face.

quotes.text: $ hf download jkobject/scPRINT medium-v1.5.ckpt --local-dir .

steps.title: Embed and classify cells
steps.explanation: Replace my_human_anndata.h5ad with your file. The README warns this runs PCA and UMAP and may need a lot of RAM.

quotes.text: $ scprint embed --adata my_human_anndata.h5ad --ckpt_path medium-v1.5.ckpt --species "NCBITaxon:9606" --output_filename embedded.h5ad
the current version implies doing a PCA and Umap so it might need a lot of RAM if run as is

outputs: embedded.h5ad holding the cell embeddings and label predictions. The denoise and gninfer subcommands write denoised.h5ad and grn.h5ad in the same way.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
